dimensions.evidence_requirement: Repository identity and current metadata must match independently observed repository state.
Canonical machine vocabularies must be singular, closed, and consumed without divergent duplicates.
One machine-defined authority precedence model must govern conflicts and source ordering.
Every active normative record kind must satisfy its complete closed machine contract.
Required human renderings must be generated or parity-verified against canonical machine requirements.
Every declared supported work type and stack overlay must have complete executable coverage and representative scenarios.
Default v2 outputs must use runtime-neutral execution semantics with runtime adapters outside universal ownership.
Legacy 1.x and Zeref behavior must be available only through explicit versioned compatibility paths that cannot weaken controls.
Externally derived normative requirements must map to governed current official-source records and local adoption decisions.
Release-blocking adopted sources must pass currentness, supersession, and review-cadence checks.
Legal applicability must preserve publication, effective dates, transition windows, future-effective requirements, and supersession without automated compliance claims.
Applicability decisions must be deterministic, evidence-backed, and fail closed on material unknowns or conflicts.
Deterministic cross-requirement contradiction checks must block structurally provable conflicts and surface unresolved semantic conflicts for review.
Equivalent canonical inputs must produce byte-stable compiled outputs under the documented deterministic contract.
Compiled project packs must pass integrity, completeness, traceability, and tamper-detection verification.
Human and AI entrypoints must provide bounded onboarding, explainability, recovery, and representative journey evidence.
AI-facing compiled context must remain selective, provenance-preserving, size-bounded, and protected from untrusted instruction injection.
Current Shiroe adapter handoff and receipt verification must be demonstrated without treating self-attestation as independent runtime proof.
Every approved supported Python version and operating system must pass the blocking release-candidate matrix.
Canonical release-candidate benchmark and fuzz suites must pass reproducibly on the exact candidate commit.
All required CI evidence must bind to the exact candidate commit and pass without soft-failure substitution.
Release-critical evidence must be independently reproduced or explicitly remain NOT_VERIFIED when independent execution is unavailable.
Public security documentation must define supported versions and an owner-approved private vulnerability reporting path.
No open release-blocking finding may remain unresolved, accepted without explicit governance, or omitted from the release decision.
